I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Before computing them, I ran the same code on Q2, and it reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Question | Q3 answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment and its net sales | consumer, 353,588,404 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 240 |
| c. Top category and its net sales | sw, 306,179,578 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the most refunds | u89@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 229 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 679,774 |
| h. September vs August growth | 7.6% |

I applied three data fixes on top of your definitions. Without them the Q2 values didn't match:

- **Dates use Korean time (UTC+9):** The order times are stored in UTC. Splitting quarters and months by UTC date gave the wrong Q2 values; using Korean time matched them.
- **Segment names are cleaned up:** The same segment is written different ways in the data, such as `Enterprise ` (trailing space) vs `enterprise` and `SMB` vs `smb`. I trimmed spaces and lowercased them before grouping.
- **One email counts as one customer:** 300 customer records share only 250 emails; for example, u103@ex.com has 3 records. For b and f, counting by email matched Q2 (236 and 189). Counting by record gave 278 and 215.

Every Q3 paid order has at least one line item, so the average in g divides by all 1,234 orders. September (h) is up from August but still below July, which is why d is July.

STATUS: DONE
